rationale: Record per-presented-frame drag coalescing in the macOS plug-in editor host for the watched render family. The `PointerCoalescer` and its per-frame flush landed in the standalone window host and were never propagated to the plug-in host, because `PulpGpuPluginView` is a separate ObjC class from `PulpMetalView`: `mouseDragged:` called `pulp_plugin_mouse_drag` and then `request_repaint()` synchronously, per raw AppKit event. Pulp's own header records what that costs -- at 60 input events per second the app presented 2.7 frames per second while issuing ~997 repaint requests per second -- and the plug-in host is the surface a DAW user actually drags. The change is confined to Pulp-owned host input plumbing: a new portable `pulp::view::HostDragCoalescer` owning the host-side policy (fail-safe, one dirty signal per held run, flush-before-handoff ordering, counters) around the existing coalescer, both plug-in views holding drag motion and flushing once per presented frame from their CVDisplayLink callbacks before the idle pump, mouse-up flushing first, and destructors discarding rather than delivering. It adds no renderer, canvas, Skia, Graphite, Dawn, or resource implementation authority and changes no transferred slice; the standalone window host deliberately keeps its incident-hardened inline implementation so its `raw_drag_samples` counter keeps measuring what it measures today.
